story_title: As an Event Organiser or Event Coordinator, I want to view the registrations for an event I manage so that I know who is attending and how full the event is

acceptance_criteria.text: The responsible Event Organiser and the assigned Event Coordinator can view the list of registrations for their event.
Each entry shows the attendee's name, contact details, registration status and registration date.
Registered, waitlisted, withdrawn and checked-in attendees are distinguishable.
Attendees added manually on the Organiser's behalf are identifiable (see: Manually Add Attendee).
The list shows the number of active registrations against the registration capacity, and the number of attendees on the waiting list.
The list reflects registrations, withdrawals and waiting-list changes as they happen.
Given registration is not enabled for the event, when the list is opened, then it states that registration is not enabled rather than showing an empty list.
An Event Organiser cannot view the registration list of an event they are not responsible for.
Attendees, Venue Staff and Technical Support Staff cannot view the registration list.

test_cases.title: The open list shows a new registration and then its withdrawal within 15 seconds, without refreshing the page
test_cases.preconditions:
Before and after: run `npm run fixtures:spm65` (never `npx prisma db seed`, which wipes everyone's data).
Two browser windows: a normal one, and a private (incognito) one, so the two logins don't replace each other.
In the normal window, logged in as Evelyn Chen (evelyn.chen@straitsmedic.com / password123).
steps: In the normal window, click 'My Events' in the sidebar
Click 'SPM65 Live Update Workshop' in the list
Click the 'Attendees' tab, and leave this window open on it without refreshing
In the private window, go to the site (e.g. http://localhost:3000) and log in as Marcus Yeo (marcus.yeo@example.com / password123), an Attendee
Click 'Browse Events' in the sidebar
Click 'SPM65 Live Update Workshop'
Click 'Register' in the 'Your registration' card
Switch to the normal window and wait up to 15 seconds, without refreshing
Switch to the private window and click 'Withdraw' in the 'Your registration' card
Click 'Withdraw' in the dialog
Switch to the normal window and wait up to 15 seconds, without refreshing
test_cases.test_data: Event: SPM65 Live Update Workshop (capacity 5, nobody registered) | Organiser: Evelyn Chen | Attendee: Marcus Yeo
test_cases.expected_result:
Step 3: The Attendees page says '0 of 5 places taken · 0 on the waiting list' and 'No one has registered yet'.
Step 7: A green message says 'You're registered for this event.'
Step 8: Without a refresh, the list now has one row, Marcus Yeo, marcus.yeo@example.com, with the badge 'Registered' and today's date and time, and it says '1 of 5 places taken · 0 on the waiting list'.
Step 10: The dialog closes and a green message says 'You have withdrawn from this event.'
Step 11: Without a refresh, Marcus Yeo's badge is now 'Withdrawn' with a 'Withdrew' line giving today's date and time, and it says '0 of 5 places taken · 0 on the waiting list'.

open_questions: RESOLVED 2026-10-15: written after the code (branch SPM-65-View-Registration-List). Every label, message and page address in the cases is what the code shows, and the page tests (src/app/__tests__/event-attendees-page.test.tsx) render the screen with the cases' wording. Not yet clicked through by a person in a browser.

RESOLVED 2026-10-15: where the list is. The 'Attendees' tab on the event page (UI_DESIGN S-11), shown to Event Organisers and Event Coordinators. Columns 'Attendee', 'Contact', 'Status', 'Registered', oldest registration first. Contact is the attendee's email, plus their phone number when their account has one (no seeded attendee has a phone number, so the cases see the email only).

RESOLVED 2026-10-15: AC3. The existing status badges: 'Registered' (green), 'Waiting list' (amber), 'Withdrawn' (grey), 'Attended' (blue - the checked-in state; changed from green by this story so it no longer looks like 'Registered'). A withdrawn row also shows 'Withdrew <date>'.

RESOLVED 2026-10-15: AC4. A new database column records who added a registration on an attendee's behalf; the list shows 'Added by <name>' under the attendee's name. Manually Add Attendee is not built, so nothing in the app sets it yet: the fixtures set it for Anita Devi on 'SPM65 Harbourfront Seminar'. When Manually Add Attendee is built, it must record the organiser who added the attendee.

RESOLVED 2026-10-15: AC5. 'N of C places taken · W on the waiting list', or 'N registered (no capacity limit) · W on the waiting list' when no capacity is set. Places taken counts Registered and Attended, the same rule as SPM-51's capacity check and SPM-52's Registration card.

RESOLVED 2026-10-15: AC6. The tab reads the list again every 15 seconds while it is in view, and straight away when it comes back into view (decided 2026-10-15). No refresh is needed, but a change can take up to 15 seconds to appear.

RESOLVED 2026-10-15: AC6 waiting-list changes. Nobody can join or leave the waiting list from the app yet (Join and Respond to Waiting List, SPM-66), so no case moves an attendee on or off it. The list reads waiting-list registrations the same way as the others, so they will update the same way once SPM-66 is built.

RESOLVED 2026-10-15: AC7. When registration is not enabled the tab says 'Registration is not enabled for this event'. If attendees registered before it was turned off, they are still listed under that message (SPM65 Paused Forum), so the organiser does not lose sight of them.

RESOLVED 2026-10-15: AC8. The organiser who raised the event is the responsible one. Another organiser at the same client can open the event (as before) but gets 'Not authorised' on its Attendees tab; an organiser from another client cannot see the event at all. AC1 reads 'the assigned Event Coordinator', so another coordinator is refused too (SPM-65-TC10).

RESOLVED 2026-10-15: AC9. Attendees, Venue Staff and Technical Support have no 'Attendees' tab, and typing the tab's address shows 'Not authorised'. The Operations Manager and Safety Officer are refused too; the story names neither, so the unit tests cover them rather than a manual case.

RESOLVED 2026-10-15: not reachable from the screens, so covered by route tests only (src/app/api/__tests__/event-registrations-list.test.ts): calling the registrations API without logging in, and for a draft event.

RESOLVED 2026-10-15: fixtures. `npm run fixtures:spm65` (scripts/seed-spm65.ts) deletes and recreates only the six 'SPM65 …' events (seed keys spm65_*), with their registration settings and registrations, at fixed registration dates; the same events (without those) are at the end of prisma/seed.ts, and the base seed gives them no random registrations. No pinned reference numbers: find each event by title. The open events' registration runs to 31 Dec 2027, so SPM-65-TC04 holds until then.
